title: Tibetan Udānavarga — Derge Kangyur Toh 326
scope: Historical Tibetan counterparts of Pāli Dhammapada 1–43 only.
editorial_policy: These are historical Tibetan Udānavarga witnesses, not new Tibetan translations of Pāli. Folio/line citations identify the Derge source. Sanskrit parallel numbers do not prescribe Tibetan numbering or stanza order. Reading line breaks follow shad-delimited pādas and are editorial; physical folio line breaks remain in the raw excerpts. Original spelling before a correction suggestion is retained. Related passages are labelled partial; an unfound counterpart is not filled with a translation.

sources.title: Udānavarga, Ched du brjod pa’i tshoms, Derge Kangyur Toh 326 (mdo sde, sa), vol 72, ff 209a.1–253a.7
sources.license: Public domain, as declared by the source repository.
sources.attribution: ཆོས་ཀྱི་འབྱུང་གནས། [1721–31], བཀའ་འགྱུར་སྡེ་དགེ་པར་མ།. Etexts from UVA, BDRC OCR, ACIP, and Adarsha combined and further proofread by Esukhia on behalf of Barom Theksum Choling,2012–2018.
sources.edition_note: Based on the Library of Congress Derge Kangyur (BDRC W4CZ5369). The source preserves archaic spellings and carving mistakes. Its README flags potential errors and correction suggestions. No fresh transcription from scans was undertaken here.
sources.translator_attribution: Rin chen mchog with the Indian scholar conventionally identified as Vidyākaraprabhā; revised by dPal brtsegs. The Derge colophon at253a.7 spells the Indian name བིདྱཱ་པྲ་བྷ་ཀ་ར; this spelling is not silently normalized.

sources.title: Udānavarga, Bibliotheca Polyglotta, University of Oslo
sources.role: Scholarly Sanskrit–Tibetan alignment and bibliographic check. The first ten Apramāda verses were checked against the native Tibetan source. Sanskrit text is based on Bernhard 1965; Tibetan reference is Kg mdo sde sa 209a1–253a7.
sources.license: No license assumed for the modern alignment. It is cited as a research reference; display text is taken from the public-domain Esukhia source.

sources.title: W. Woodville Rockhill, Udânavarga: a collection of verses from the Buddhist canon (London: Trübner,1883)
sources.role: Independent Tibetan verse numbering and Pāli concordance, especially chapter 28.37/Pāli 17 and28.39/Pāli 18 (p 139; concordance p 217). OCR is retained only in bounded research excerpts; no English translation is displayed.
sources.license: Public domain (published1883; translator died1914). Archive OCR is an imperfect mechanical derivative; Tibetan text is not taken from OCR.

sources.title: Ānandajoti Bhikkhu, A Comparative Edition of the Dhammapada, chapters 1–3
sources.role: Starting Pāli–Sanskrit Uv correspondence supplied by the main researcher; confirmed against the native Tibetan text rather than treating Sanskrit numbering as Tibetan numbering.
sources.license: Research reference only; no edition text copied into this Tibetan dataset.

readings.note: Sanskrit groups the bad-roof similes before the good-roof similes; this Derge Tibetan source pairs them. This is its good-roof/desire counterpart of Sanskrit Uv 31.17. Rockhill’s English sequence lacks this exact good-roof/desire stanza: his 31.14 instead follows the bad-roof/passions stanza. No Rockhill verse number is assigned to this Derge reading.

No sufficiently close Tibetan counterpart was located in the bounded comparison. The Mind chapter contains other verses about guarding mind, but they are not substituted for this verse. This is not proof that no parallel exists anywhere in Tibetan literature.
